tools.name: log_expense
tools.title: Log expense
tools.description: Record ONE purchase, bill, or receipt. Negative amount = refund to the same category. NEVER use this for bank-statement rows or any batch of 3+ records: use import_transactions with the whole array instead (one-by-one logging hits the per-turn tool limit).

amount.description: Amount spent in the original currency. Negative = refund.

currency.description: 3-letter ISO currency code (EUR, USD, UAH, AED, ...). Omit to use the user's base currency.

category.description: Omit only if nothing fits; defaults to 'other'.

date.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today.

price.description: Line price in the receipt's currency

items.description: Receipt line items, when logging from a receipt photo.

entity.description: Override the account's default scope, e.g. a personal dinner paid with the business card.

tools.name: log_income
tools.title: Log income
tools.description: Record incoming money: salary, client payment, gift.

amount.description: Amount received in the original currency.

currency.description: 3-letter ISO currency code (EUR, USD, UAH, AED, ...). Omit to use the user's base currency.

merchant.description: Payer / source, e.g. client or employer name.

date.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today.

entity.description: Override the account's default scope, e.g. a client payment landing on a personal card.

tools.name: get_accounts
tools.title: Accounts & net worth
tools.description: All accounts with computed balances (latest snapshot + tracked flows) and total net worth in the base currency. Optionally filtered to personal or business scope.

entity.description: Only accounts of this scope. Omit for all.

tools.name: log_transfer
tools.title: Log transfer
tools.description: Move money between OWN accounts: card to brokerage, cash withdrawal, currency exchange. Never counted as spending or income.

received_currency.description: Currency arriving, for cross-currency transfers. Default: the destination account's currency.

date.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today.

tools.name: import_transactions
tools.title: Bulk import
tools.description: Import bank-statement / statement-screenshot rows in bulk. ALWAYS send the ENTIRE statement as ONE call with the full transactions array (up to 500 rows) - never split into chunks, never log rows one-by-one via log_expense. If one statement truly cannot fit in a single call, EVERY row of EVERY chunk must carry external_id (bank reference; or a statement-scoped row id such as '2026-09:r017' - bare row numbers repeat in every statement) - rows without external_id are keyed by amount+date+occurrence WITHIN one call, so identical rows arriving in different calls are indistinguishable from re-imports. Safe to re-run: keyed rows are skipped, a hand-logged twin is merged into the bank row instead of duplicating, and repeated purchases (same merchant and amount on different days, or twice the same day) import normally. Unknown categories become 'other'. Pass statement_total to get a reconciliation check. Sign convention: negative amount = money out, positive = money in.

statement_total.description: Signed sum of ALL rows in the source statement, for reconciliation.

dry_run.description: Preview only: report what would be imported/skipped/merged without writing anything.

date.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today.

currency.description: 3-letter ISO currency code (EUR, USD, UAH, AED, ...). Omit to use the user's base currency.

external_id.description: Bank transaction reference - the strongest dedup key. Without one, a statement-scoped row id ('2026-09:r017'). If absent, the server derives a stable key from amount + date + position.

force.description: Import even if a similar row exists. Use ONLY when a previous response's hint asked to re-send this row. Exact external_id duplicates are still skipped.

entity.description: Scope override for THIS row, e.g. a personal dinner inside a business-account statement. Default: the account's entity.

tools.name: get_summary
tools.title: Spending summary
tools.description: Totals for a period, computed server-side in the user's base currency. Breaks down expenses (default) or income: 'how much did I spend on X in July', 'what does my June income consist of'. Supports category drill-down (category=subscriptions + group_by=merchant), exclusions (exclude_categories), week-by-week views (group_by=week), comparison with the period before (compare=previous: 'how does this week compare to last week') and totals in another currency (currency=USD).

period.description: YYYY-MM or YYYY. Defaults to the current month.

from.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today.

to.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today.

type.description: Which side the groups break down. Default: expense. Use income for 'where does my income come from'.

compare.description: previous: also return the period before (the previous month, year or same-length window; for a period still running, the same number of days of the one before) and each category's or merchant's change.

currency.description: Report in this currency instead of the base: every record is converted at its own date's rate (e.g. USD totals for peso spending).

category.description: Only this category, e.g. subscriptions with group_by=merchant to see what the subscriptions consist of.

exclude_categories.description: Drop these categories from totals and groups, e.g. ['business'] for personal stats without business-categorized records.

entity.description: personal or business only. Omit for everything.

trend_months.description: Month-by-month expense and income for the last N months instead of one period (optionally one expense category or one entity): 'how did my spending change since spring'.

tools.name: get_transactions
tools.title: List transactions
tools.description: Find records: 'what was that 40 eur charge', recent spending, by category or merchant. Newest first. total = all matches; when has_more is true, call again with offset=next_offset to page (never treat count as the total).

from.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today.

to.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today.

tools.name: update_transaction
tools.title: Update transaction
tools.description: Fix a logged record: wrong category, amount, merchant, date, account, personal/business scope, or type. type=transfer + counter_account converts a mislogged row into a transfer between own accounts (e.g. a cash withdrawal into a transfer to Cash). counter_transaction_id instead GLUES TWO EXISTING rows (one expense + one income on different own accounts) into ONE transfer - use it when a currency exchange, own-account top-up, or cash withdrawal produced two separate rows. Category fixes on rows with a merchant are remembered: future bank syncs of that merchant reuse your category.

currency.description: 3-letter ISO currency code (EUR, USD, UAH, AED, ...). Omit to use the user's base currency.

date.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today.

type.description: Convert the record's type. transfer additionally needs counter_account.

counter_account.description: The OTHER own account of a transfer (for an expense row: where the money went, e.g. Cash). With type=transfer it converts the row; on an existing transfer it re-points the destination.

counter_transaction_id.description: Merge ANOTHER existing row into this one as the second leg of a transfer between own accounts. One row must be an expense, the other an income, on different accounts (any currencies). The other row is absorbed: its account/amount/currency become the counter leg and its bank reference is preserved, so re-syncs and re-imports do not duplicate it.

account.description: Move the row to this own account (see get_accounts).

tools.name: delete_transactions
tools.title: Delete transactions
tools.description: Delete wrongly logged transactions by id (from get_transactions): one, or many in ONE call with every id in ids. Never one call per row: one-by-one deletion hits the per-turn tool limit.

tools.name: set_budget
tools.title: Set budget
tools.description: Monthly spending cap, overall or per category, in the user's base currency.

category.description: Omit for the overall monthly budget.

tools.name: get_budget_progress
tools.title: Budget progress
tools.description: Current month (user's timezone): spent vs cap for every budget, plus days left in the month. Budgets track PERSONAL spending only; business-scope transactions never count against them. log_expense and import_transactions return budget_alerts when they push a budget over its cap.

tools.name: get_recurring
tools.title: Recurring payments
tools.description: Subscriptions, rent, bills and other payments that repeat: the ones the user saved (set_recurring) and the ones found in their records (charges at one merchant that repeat weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly at a steady amount; evidence=seen_once marks a single recent charge of a subscription service, cadence unknown). Each with amount, cadence, next expected date and monthly cost in the base currency; plus the monthly and yearly total (saved and repeating ones) and what is coming up in the next 30 days. Call it for 'what subscriptions do I pay', 'my fixed costs', 'what bills are coming'. Found ones are suggestions: offer to save the ones the user confirms (set_recurring).

include_stopped.description: Also list found series that seem to have stopped (no charge since the expected date).

tools.name: set_recurring
tools.title: Save a recurring payment
tools.description: Save, change or remove a payment the user expects again (a subscription, rent, a bill). Saved ones show in get_recurring and in the email summary's 'Coming up'. With auto_log=true the expense is written on each date automatically: only for a fixed amount charged in this currency, and only for users who log by hand (refused while a bank or ZenMoney sync is connected: the sync brings the charge). A statement import merges an auto-logged row with the bank's row of the same amount within two days. Saving again under the same name changes it; remove=true deletes it (expenses already logged stay).

name.description: The payment as the user calls it, e.g. Netflix, Rent.

merchant.description: The merchant as the records spell it (a found payment's name, e.g. 'LANDLORD SL'), when the user's name differs: links the saved payment to its charges.

amount.description: Amount per charge. Required for a new one.

currency.description: 3-letter ISO currency code (EUR, USD, UAH, AED, ...). Omit to use the user's base currency.

cadence.description: How often it is charged. Required for a new one.

next_date.description: Next expected charge, YYYY-MM-DD. Required for a new one. A past date moves to the next one on or after today; nothing is logged for past dates.

account.description: Account the auto-logged expense goes to. Default: Manual.

auto_log.description: Write the expense automatically on each date.

remove.description: Delete the saved payment with this name.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.title: Get settings
tools.description: Signed-in account email (which account is connected), base currency, timezone, the email summary choice and the server version.

tools.name: update_settings
tools.title: Update settings
tools.description: Change base currency (recomputes all historical stats at each transaction's original date rate), timezone, or the email summary (email_digest).

base_currency.description: 3-letter ISO currency code (EUR, USD, UAH, AED, ...). Omit to use the user's base currency.

email_digest.description: Email summary to the sign-in address: weekly (Mondays), monthly (on the 1st) or off. Set weekly/monthly ONLY after the user explicitly said yes; a confirmation with this month so far goes out at once.

tools.name: delete_all_data
tools.title: Delete all data
tools.description: Erase the user profile and ALL financial data permanently (GDPR). For removing a single money account use manage_account action=delete instead. Requires confirm='DELETE'.

tools.name: manage_account
tools.title: Manage accounts
tools.description: Money accounts (bank, card, cash, investment), one action per call. create: name, type, currency (entity optional). update: account plus new_name, type, currency or entity (history stays; an entity change affects future rows). set_balance: account, amount, optional currency and date: the REAL balance from the bank app at the end of that date; balances are this snapshot plus later flows. merge: source into target, moving every row, dropping duplicates (same type, currency, amount, date within dedup_window_days; the row with a bank reference wins) and deleting source; typical for a statement-import account and a bank-sync account of the same bank; run dry_run=true first and show the counts. delete: account with its snapshots; delete_transactions=true when it still has rows; delete_all_data erases everything. Transfers between own accounts never count as spending.

account.description: update, set_balance, delete: the account's name (see get_accounts).

type.description: create (required), update: cash | bank | card | investment.

currency.description: create (required): main currency. update: main currency the balance is shown in. set_balance: default the account's.

entity.description: create, update: personal (default) or business, the default scope of the account's rows.

amount.description: set_balance: the balance shown by the bank or broker.

date.description: set_balance: balance as of the end of this date. Default: today.

source.description: merge: account to merge FROM (deleted afterwards).

dry_run.description: merge: preview counts without changing anything.

dedup_window_days.description: merge: duplicate match window in days, default 3; 0 = bank-reference duplicates only.

delete_transactions.description: delete: must be true when the account still has transactions.

tools.name: export_data
tools.title: Export data
tools.description: The user's data, for portability (GDPR) or a backup. what=profile: everything except the transactions as one JSON (settings, accounts with balance snapshots, budgets, saved recurring payments, the merchant category rules learned from the user's fixes, bank and ZenMoney links without tokens). what=transactions: all transactions as CSV, oldest first, with the account and the other side of transfers, up to 2000 rows per call: when a second text block reports has_more, call again with offset=next_offset and the same filters.

entity.description: transactions: one scope only, e.g. business rows for the accountant.

offset.description: transactions: skip this many rows (paging). Default 0.

tools.name: zenmoney
tools.title: ZenMoney sync
tools.description: Read-only sync with a ZenMoney account (zenmoney.app international and zenmoney.ru both work; the backend is detected). action=paste_token stores the user's personal ZenMoney API token: free at zerro.app (log in choosing YOUR ZenMoney version, then open zerro.app/token and copy it). action=sync pulls transactions, accounts and balances (incremental, safe to re-run; the first sync takes the full history unless months_back is set; dry_run previews; unmapped ZenMoney tags land in 'other' for the user to review). action=status: connection health and synced accounts. action=set_account_sync with account + enabled turns ONE account on or off, e.g. when the same bank also syncs from another source (relay any overlap_warnings). action=disconnect removes the link and token; imported rows stay.

account.description: set_account_sync: account name or id (see action=status).

enabled.description: set_account_sync: true = resume syncing this account, false = stop.

dry_run.description: sync: preview transaction changes without writing them.

months_back.description: sync, first run only: import history no older than this many months.

tools.name: bank
tools.title: Bank sync
tools.description: Read-only sync with a real bank via open banking (Enable Banking, EU/UK/EEA). If the user's country or bank is not listed, stop and import a statement instead (import_transactions). Flow: action=list_banks with the country (and optional search) for the exact bank name; action=start with bank_name + country returns an authorize_url the user opens and approves at the bank; when they are done, action=sync (first sync takes months_back of history, default 3; later ones are incremental; the server also syncs healthy connections daily). action=status: health, consent expiry, synced accounts. action=set_account_sync with account + enabled turns ONE account on or off (relay any overlap_warnings: the same bank via ZenMoney duplicates). action=disconnect revokes the session; imported rows stay. One bank connection at a time.

country.description: 2-letter country code (FI, DE, FR, ...). Required for list_banks and start.

search.description: list_banks: case-insensitive filter on bank names.

bank_name.description: start: exact bank name as list_banks returned it.

account.description: set_account_sync: account name or id (see action=status).

enabled.description: set_account_sync: true = resume syncing this account, false = stop.

dry_run.description: sync: preview changes without writing them.

months_back.description: sync, first run only: months of history to request. Default 3.

resources.name: dashboard
resources.description: MyFinance MCP dashboard: budgets, trends, summary, accounts
